subject: Next steps — spend slab authorization & $/1M token rate check
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@finlytics.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, May 4, 2028 at 5:02 PM -0700
Subject: Next steps — spend slab authorization & $/1M token rate check

Hi Ethan — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and clear next steps so we keep momentum: 

What I heard from your team:
- Pilot scope: customer support summarization + SLA-aware routing for top two enterprise customers (approx 15–20k end users).
- Rough runtime profile: short prompts (~75 tokens) + longer context retrieval (~350 tokens) leading to mixed seq lengths.
- Goal: validate monthly spend band and procurement path to get a PO in place by mid-June.

Immediate asks / next steps (from our side):
1) Please confirm your expected monthly token consumption range for the pilot (low / likely / high). A single-line range is fine (e.g., 5M / 12M / 30M).
2) Procurement trigger: what spend level requires a formal PO vs. credit-card onboarding?
3) Any paperwork we should pre-fill? I attached a simple spend worksheet (FinLytics_Spend_Template.xlsx) to make the math easier.

On our side we'll:
- Karthik will propose two priced options (short commit vs. reserved capacity) with $/1M-token math and estimated monthly totals.
- Share PO-onboarding checklist and supplier docs (attached).

If you can reply with the three items above by end of day tomorrow we can get a draft SOW+PO to your procurement team.

Thanks —
Jasmine Liu
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.com
(Attachment: FinLytics_Spend_Template.xlsx)
From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@finlytics.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@finlytics.com
Date: Fri, May 5, 2028 at 8:12 AM -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps — spend slab authorization & $/1M token rate check

Thanks Jasmine — good demo and appreciate the clear recap. Answers inline: 

1) Monthly token consumption (pilot estimate):
- Low: ~8M tokens/mo (light usage week)
- Likely: ~28–35M tokens/mo
- High: up to ~60M tokens/mo (if we open to more customers during ramp)

2) Procurement trigger:
- <$10,000/month -> procurement allows credit-card pay; finance handles supplier onboarding later.
- >=$10,000/month -> requires formal PO and supplier onboarding (legal + tax forms).
- >=$25,000/month -> needs VP approval and additional security attestation (they flagged the SLA/uptime requirement).

3) Paperwork: procurement asked for: vendor W-9 (we have it), supplier security questionnaire, and a short vendor onboarding packet. If you can share a sample PO and net-terms, that will speed approval.

For budgeting, we are targeting spend in the $8k–$18k/month band for the pilot — if unit economics can land near $300–$375 per 1M tokens we should be able to get through procurement without senior exec signoff.

Linking procurement here so they see our cadence.

—Ethan
Ethan Cole
Head of Integrations — FinLytics
ethan.cole@finlytics.com
(Procurement: procurement@finlytics.com)
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@finlytics.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Fri, May 5, 2028 at 8:55 AM -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps — spend slab authorization & $/1M token rate check

Thanks Ethan — helpful numbers. Sharing two pragmatic pricing scenarios you can present to Finance/Procurement; both assume typical production optimizations (KV caching on retrieval paths, request batching, and a small model-quantization profile for summarization). Estimates are conservative.

Scenario A — Pilot (no reserved capacity)
- Unit price: $395 per 1M tokens
- Typical monthly tokens (likely): 30M → estimated monthly = 30 * 395 = $11,850
- PO threshold: we can start with credit card if under $10k; for the numbers above procurement will want a PO.
- Terms: month-to-month; 30-day notice for cancellation.

Scenario B — 6–12 month reserved band (recommended if you expect 30M+/mo)
- Unit price: $310 per 1M tokens (10% invoice-level discount + lower execution cost due to reserved GPU pools)
- Typical monthly tokens (likely): 30M → estimated monthly = 30 * 310 = $9,300
- Minimum commit: 6 months; single PO covering first quarter recommended.
- Additional: optional 5% adoption credit if you hit >40M tokens in any month during the first 90 days.

Notes on procurement lanes:
- If FinLytics requires the PO to be >$25k to route to VP, we can split the initial commit into quarterly POs to keep per-PO amounts within your procurement cadence.
- We can also set a soft cap routing rule in the contract that alerts both finance teams at 80% of the committed slab.

Attachments: I included a quick one-page math sheet (we referenced Jasmine's template) and a supplier onboarding checklist (Redwood_PO_Onboarding.pdf).

If either scenario looks reasonable I can draft the pricing exhibit earlier today and send to your procurement team for intake.

—Karthik Iyer
Head of Revenue Operations — Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
(Attachment: Redwood_PO_Onboarding.pdf)
From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@finlytics.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@finlytics.com
Date: Fri, May 5, 2028 at 9:18 AM -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps — spend slab authorization & $/1M token rate check

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Karthik — Scenario B looks like the one we should aim for. A few procurement notes from our side: 

- Procurement requires a draft SOW + pricing exhibit before they start the vendor onboarding packet. If you can send a one-page SOW (scope + expected monthly token band) and a simple pricing exhibit with the line items as you outlined, procurement will queue the supplier packet.
- Net terms: procurement prefers Net30; we can request Net45 in special cases but it's slower.
- PO routing rules: we will need the first PO to be aligned with the quarter boundaries. Ideally we keep the first PO at ~ $28k (covers quarter at Scenario B rates for our expected ramp) so it sits cleanly with our internal budget cadence.

Next steps for Redwood:
1) Karthik / Jasmine — please send a one-page SOW + pricing exhibit (Scenario B preferred) and a sample PO template.
2) I will route those to procurement and loop back with required legal redlines (if any).

If you send the docs today we should be able to get procurement intake started and get a PO issued within 2–3 weeks, assuming no legal redlines.

Thanks —
Ethan
(Attachment: none)
